newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent and paper trade higher in thin business.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent and paper trade higher in thin business.

text.p: North Sea crude markets traded higher on Thursday as sellers breathed easy in the wake of a hefty mid-week clearout of cargoes, traders said.
Paper markets were also stronger, reacting to a morning bid at July Brent -55 cents for a cargo loading June 22-26, some 15 cents stronger than the previous Brent deal, which was on Wednesday
"It seems to have solidified a little, though it was very quiet today," said one trader.

Only one physical deal was confirmed, a Gullfaks C loading June 29/July 01, at dated Brent +10 cents, though there were rumours of an Ekofisk or Statfjord traded out of Norway. The last Gullfaks deal seen was on Tuesday at dated evens.
"Yesterday's buying moved things up a little," said one trader. "We seem to have had a bit of clearing out at the end of the month."
At least 10 North Sea cargoes, mostly Statfjords and Ekofisks, were snapped up on Wednesday, reducing the June overhang of non-Brent cargoes to around a dozen.

Much June Brent remains unspoken for but traders said steep contango may have encouraged some to push material into storage. And while the transatlantic arb appears tight, a ULCC of Brent crude has been fixed to head west on June 17, easing the supply situation.

However few believed there was significant upside strength to Brent and with many market participants heading today to an industry get-together in Norway, trade was thin enough to allow numbers to rise easily.

"The July loading programmes are coming up over the next few days and people have started to look to them," said one trader. "I believe they'll be sizeable and we can expect to be in contango for some time to come."
Two Brent cargoes loading June 27-29 were kept from the paper chains on Thursday, traders said.
While paper markets followed physical upwards, business was thin and secretive.
One July/August spread was heard done at -30 cents, but numbers later firmed. Short-term swaps also improved, with a CFD for next week (June 16-20) done at August Brent -65 cents.
The following week (June 23-27) was done at August Brent -57 cents and July 7-11 was traded at August Brent -42 cents.
Russian Urals crude was steady with trade stifled by talk of deals done at levels too great for the rest of the market.

Traders reported hearing values of Dated -$1/$1.05 agreed between trading houses for the million-barrel Biruinta loading June 27-29 and a discount of around $1 for the million-barrel Cuban loading June 22-24.
"At these kinds of levels we've washed our hands of it and started to look at other grades," said one buyer for a refinery.
Asian buying was believed easing the supply glut in West African grades, but Nigerian cargoes were not those attracting interest.

Some U.S. buying was reported, with a Qua Iboe traded yesterday at Dated +26 cents yesterday and again at Dated +23 cents, but generally purchasers appeared happy to wait till cargoes became distressed.
Traders predicted numbers would fall further to clear out the estimated six million barrel overhang for June.
-- Sean Maguire, London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
